messages:
jess: Customer on Dedicated hit an error when using structured_output/jsonmode + pydantic validation. They get a 502 from our API because the model returned an odd escaped sequence that breaks the parser. Repro & logs below.

jess: REPRO (customer provided)
```
POST /v1/responses
{
  "model": "open-llm-v1",
  "jsonmode": true,
  "input": "Summarize actions",
  "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "summary": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": ["summary"],
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
}

MODEL OUTPUT (streamed final chunk):
...
"summary": "Fixed issue with auth...\u2026 deployed to prod",
}
```

jess: Notice the model inserted an escaped unicode ellipsis (\u2026) inside the string and we ended up with a trailing comma after the object. Pydantic rejects this and our structured_output parsing layer returns a 502 upstream.

oliver: Can you confirm which SDK + runtime the customer used? streaming vs non-streaming?

jess: They hit hosted API via Python SDK v0.9, using streaming=False (single response). Pydantic v1.10 strict config on their side. They said the SDK tried to parse but failed.

mia: Two quick thoughts: 1) The trailing comma is a model-generation bug — we should treat as invalid JSON from the model and surface a clearer 4xx to the user instead of a 502. 2) The escaped ellipsis is valid JSON (\u2026) but combined with trailing comma breaks parsing. We could add a linting pre-parse step to detect trailing commas and common stray tokens and return structured_error with example fix.

oliver: +1 on better error mapping. If we map model-JSON-parse failures -> 400 with "model_output_invalid_json" and attach the raw snippet, it helps users debug and avoids 502 alarms. I'll triage the runtime layer that wraps pydantic.

eng-ml-oncall-bot: Ticket ENGML-4321 created: \"structured_output parser: classify model-invalid-json -> 400; add lightweight sanitizer opt-in\". Priority: P2.

jess: Customer asked for ETA; can we give an interim workaround?

mia: Workaround: ask them to set jsonmode=false and run their own tolerant post-processing OR use a relaxed JSON pre-cleaner we can share: strip trailing commas, ensure top-level braces matched, unescape stray control chars. Warn them it may mask model bugs.

oliver: I'm going to reproduce with their payload + simulated model chunks (include trailing comma + \u2026). If I can trigger same failure locally I'll propose a small fix in parser: detect trailing comma and try a single-pass rectify before handing to pydantic.

jess: Thanks. I've told customer we have a ticket and a suggested workaround. Will follow up with ETA once oliver posts repro. :thumbsup:

eng-ml-oncall-bot: Assigned to oliver; watcher: mia, jess.
